title: s-wave: gap magnitude, symmetry and sign
summary: Separate a full gap from A1g symmetry and sign-preserving pairing, using explicit models and experimental criteria.

review.scope: Selected Anderson scan, Mishra author manuscript, original MgB2 measurement text and published hydride passages, plus scoped historical checks and independent symmetry/response illustrations. Follow-up checks official D4h/C4h character tables, BCS pp.1182–1183/1186, Anderson pp.26/29 and Mishra v1 pp.1–2; local quadrature and nonuniform-gap counterexamples remain model-scoped.
limitations: Full scientific acceptance, complete final-version comparisons and raw-data review remain open.
Imposed-gap spectra do not establish unchanged self-consistent Tc under disorder.
The clean angular heat-jump example is not a disorder calculation; independent-band DOS omits phase-sensitive interband processes.
The aluminum measurement range and hydride synthesis/pressure scales are not interchangeable with a superconducting transition criterion.
A1g labeling here requires D4h; the uniform imposed-gap spectral identity does not extend to arbitrary site-dependent pairing or establish unchanged self-consistent Tc.

claims.statement: An isotropic, sign-preserving spin-singlet gap is the conventional s-wave reference. Three questions must nevertheless be separated: whether quasiparticles are fully gapped, how the order parameter transforms under crystal symmetry, and whether it changes sign between parts of the Fermi surface. A full gap answers the first question within the measurement's resolution; it does not settle the other two.

claims.statement: For a crystal with D4h (4/mmm) point-group symmetry, A1g denotes the fully symmetric even-parity representation. It permits a constant gap but also higher harmonics and accidental nodes. The centrosymmetric tetragonal group C4h (4/m) instead labels its fully symmetric representation Ag; use the actual crystal point group. In multiband systems, fully open gaps can have opposite signs on different sheets; see the separate s± entry. Identifying an s-wave state also does not, by itself, identify its microscopic pairing interaction.

claims.statement: The equilibrium, single-band, isotropic, constant-density-of-states weak-coupling BCS model gives $2\Delta(0)/(k_BT_c)\simeq3.528$ and $\Delta C/(\gamma T_c)\simeq1.426$, with $\gamma$ the normal electronic heat-capacity coefficient. These are limiting benchmarks, not mandatory ratios for every s-wave material. The existing independent gap and entropy checks establish these model limits; strong coupling, multiband structure and anisotropy require their own calculation.

claims.statement: Rotations by $\pi/2$, reflections and inversion leave this function unchanged. For $|r|<1$ it is positive everywhere; at $|r|=1$ four zeros touch the Fermi surface without sign reversal; for $|r|>1$ there are eight sign-changing nodes. Their presence changes with a parameter rather than being required by A1g symmetry. This global fourfold example is distinct from Mishra and colleagues' local twofold harmonic on a selected off-center pocket.

claims.statement: Independent angular sums and a thermal-kernel quadrature verify five cases. At $r=0.6$ the gap remains nodeless, while the jump is about $0.933$ rather than $1.426$. This shows why applying the isotropic ratio as a symmetry test can fail. It is a clean separable-model result, not a disorder simulation or a measured sample value. The cited BCS paper provides the underlying mean-field context; the angular calculation is our independent illustration.

claims.statement: For a real symmetric normal Hamiltonian $h$ and an imposed uniform real gap, the block matrix $\mathcal H=\begin{pmatrix}h&\Delta I\\\Delta I&-h\end{pmatrix}$ has energies $\pm\sqrt{\epsilon_n^2+\Delta^2}$. Six small-matrix checks confirm this relation with different scalar site potentials. It does not prove an unchanged self-consistent $T_c$: the normal eigenvalues, density of states and pairing matrix elements can change. Anderson's argument pairs exact time-reversed states; it is not a blanket guarantee against all chemical disorder, localization or magnetic scattering. This spectral identity relies on the imposed gap being a scalar multiple of the identity. For a site-dependent real gap matrix $D$, the squared block Hamiltonian contains $hD-Dh$ in its off-diagonal block. Two explicit nonuniform-gap counterexamples verify a nonzero commutator and the failure of a naive pairing of normal-state eigenvalues with site gaps; they do not solve the gap equation.

claims.statement: A magnitude-sensitive quasiparticle spectrum cannot generally determine an interband sign. Six independent-band, broadened-DOS comparisons give identical spectra after reversing one band's gap sign. This deliberately excludes interband scattering and coherent phase-sensitive tunneling. Measurements sensitive to phase or sign need their own geometry and matrix-element analysis. Low-temperature activation alone also cannot distinguish an isotropic gap from a smaller nonzero gap minimum.

claims.statement: Hebel and Slichter's aluminum experiment used field cycling: nuclear spins relaxed in the superconducting state but were read out in the normal state. Its 0.94–4.2 K interval is a measurement range, not a range of transition temperatures. Nuclear relaxation tests a response with coherence effects; observing or missing a peak alone does not measure relative signs between bands. Only the original abstract has been checked here.

claims.statement: For lanthanum superhydrides, Somayazulu's sample A had room-temperature pressures of 188 GPa before and 196 GPa after cycling; pressure at the resistance change was not directly measured. The published account distinguishes four-probe data from contact-sensitive pseudo-four-probe configurations and mixed phases. Drozdov's later study reports additional field and isotope evidence, defines $T_c$ by resistance onset, and states that magnetization of its small samples remained unresolved. Neither transport report is a phase-sensitive measurement of gap sign.

claims.statement: Mishra and colleagues show node lifting in a model with weak pointlike scatterers treated in the Born approximation. Their single-sheet calculation can suppress $T_c$ too strongly; additional bands change that balance, while interband scattering cannot generally be discarded. This supports a conditional explanation of activated behavior after disorder, not the rule that disorder always preserves or improves s-wave superconductivity.

claims.statement: The ideal isotope value $\alpha=-d\ln T_c/d\ln M=1/2$ assumes a harmonic phonon scale and otherwise mass-independent model parameters. Sulfur-hydride isotope observations support phonon involvement within their experimental context. For lanthanum hydrides, the published methods discuss different hydride/deuteride phase mixtures and zero-point/anharmonic stability effects. Matching pressure, phase and preparation is therefore essential before interpreting a mass derivative.
